ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: Read the figure. In the figure, line segments 1, 2, 3, and 4 are all ocean currents in this ocean. <image1> If currents 2 and 3 flow in exactly opposite directions, which current’s sea area has stronger vertical upwelling?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: The figure shows the Indian Ocean region, with the east coast of Africa on the left; the equator 0° horizontal line and the 60°E meridian are shown in the figure; the lower part is labeled “South Equatorial Warm Current,” and line segment 3 is located near the South Equatorial Warm Current; line segment 1 is located in the sea area near the east coast of Africa and Somalia; line segment 2 is in the western North Indian Ocean; line segment 4 is in the eastern North Indian Ocean. Then reason: Current 3 corresponds to the South Equatorial Warm Current, which usually flows westward. The question says currents 2 and 3 flow in exactly opposite directions, so current 2 should be the eastward-flowing monsoon current formed in the North Indian Ocean in summer under the influence of the southwest monsoon. When the southwest monsoon prevails in summer, seawater along the Somali coast is affected by offshore transport, and compensating upwelling is strong; this sea area corresponds to current 1 in the figure. Therefore, the current with stronger vertical upwelling is current 1.
